# adervec's apps

> Free, open-source, local-first web apps by one maker, built with Claude Code. Each runs entirely in the browser
> with no account and no server of ours; data stays on the device and, if the reader signs in, in their own
> Google Drive app folder. Take whatever you like: the code, the ideas, the standards (licences below).

## Apps

- [GymTracker](https://adervec.github.io/GymTracker315/): A whole gym logbook in one HTML file — lifts, cardio, plans, and progress. Features: Adaptive workout plans and a fast set logger; Picker-driven equipment setup: barbell, dumbbell, kettlebell, landmine…; Per-exercise reference media and baked-in coaching guides; Biometrics, wearable recovery metrics, and Strava reconciliation; Cloud sync via Google Drive, Dropbox, or OneDrive; Offline-first — everything lives in your browser storage. Source: https://github.com/adervec/GymTracker315 (MIT).
- [Tachyread](https://adervec.github.io/Tachyread/): Speed reading one word at a time — RSVP on an optimal recognition point, up to ~1500 WPM. Features: Import TXT, DOCX, PDF, EPUB — or OCR-grab text from images; ~30 themes and animated reader faces; Listen mode: text-to-speech rendered ahead and pulled to your phone; Trackyread: a reading log of every book, with notes and a fading-memory check; Typing and speaking minigames, audiobook recording; Measured reading stats and an editable table of contents. Source: https://github.com/adervec/Tachyread (MIT).
- [ChessRetabled](https://adervec.github.io/ChessRetabled/): A cel-shaded chess club in the browser — bots, lessons, puzzles, and 56 games. Features: 12 Stockfish-powered characters, 250 to 2850 Elo; 37 validated tactics puzzles with rated training; Academy courses and practice-arena endgame drills; 56 games — board, cards, logic — each with a strategy guide; Level, XP, streaks, and personal ratings; Full offline play once installed. Source: https://github.com/adervec/ChessRetabled (GPL-3.0).
- [GuitarPicker](https://adervec.github.io/GuitarPicker/): Zero-build guitar school — note highway, tuner, karaoke, and a synthesized backing band. Features: Streaming note highway with per-note grading; Live tuner across 59 instruments and their tunings; 45+ public-domain songs, each with a synthesized backing band; Karaoke with word-by-word lyrics and pitch scoring; Practice mode, MIDI input, MusicXML import, sight-reading; Song editor, record-and-transcribe, theory games, courses. Source: https://github.com/adervec/GuitarPicker (MIT).
- [Black Mirror Bike Ride](https://adervec.github.io/BlackMirrorBikeRide/): A homebrew Zwift — your real trainer over Bluetooth, low-poly worlds, real GPX routes. Features: Reads power and heart rate over Web Bluetooth — zero drivers; A proper physics model behind every ride; Build your own low-poly 3D worlds; GPX import plus 34 bundled routes (~660 km); Replay, ride history, and ghosts. Source: https://github.com/adervec/BlackMirrorBikeRide (MIT).
- [Bodybuilding Progress Coach](https://adervec.github.io/BodybuildingProgressCoach/): Honest physique and posing tracking from your own photos — scored against the classics. Features: On-device pose analysis — nothing uploaded; Objective symmetry and proportion geometry first, opinion second; Per-division posing technique (24 mandatories) and live mirror practice; Body-composition trends corroborate the photos; Aligned progress timelapses. Source: https://github.com/adervec/BodybuildingProgressCoach (see LICENSE).
- [Handwriting Helper](https://adervec.github.io/HandwritingHelper/): Photograph a page of handwriting and get honest, measured scores — then drill. Features: Per-line scores: slant, baseline, size, spacing, pen control, legibility; Right or left hand, print or cursive, plus mirror-prime mode; 38 drills with printable guide sheets in true size; Review scan batches as a gallery, with duplicate detection; Streaks, trends, and full history. Source: https://github.com/adervec/HandwritingHelper (MIT).
- [MicroMiniger](https://adervec.github.io/MicroMiniger/): A miniature-collection manager — paint queue, photo studio, and offline photo-to-3D. Features: Rich per-mini metadata, kitbash-aware, with provenance and value; Kanban paint queue, paint timer, deadlines; Multi-angle photos, 360° viewer, spin video and GIF export; Photo-to-3D mesh and Gaussian-splat viewer, STL/PLY export; Armies, points, and a battle log; Field-scoped search, bulk edit, CSV, one-file backup. Source: https://github.com/adervec/MicroMiniger (MIT).
- [SpeechImprover](https://adervec.github.io/SpeechImprover/): Record yourself and get ten scored attributes — then train the weak ones. Features: 962 public-domain passages, 158 exercises, 65 targeted drills; Ten attributes scored 0–100, from pace to projection; Free speaking toward a chosen target tone or emotion; Reading projects — import a document and work through it passage by passage; Trends, an activity heatmap, A/B compare, AI-coach export. Source: https://github.com/adervec/SpeechImprover (MIT).
- [Mise](https://adervec.github.io/Mise/): An interactive cookbook you can run — recipes execute as live, scheduled flow charts. Features: 114 recipes plus techniques, ingredients, and equipment guides; Execute mode: station swimlanes, a moving playhead, countdowns, alarms; Voice control — play, pause, done, skip — with steps read aloud; A cook log of every finished cook, exportable; Field guides: coffee, tea, alcohol, protein prep — and a box-mix calculator. Source: https://github.com/adervec/Mise (MIT).
- [MacroTrackro](https://adervec.github.io/MacroTrackro/): Track calories and macros, and check your vitamin, supplement and pre-workout stack. Features: Food log by meal, with calories, protein, carbs and fat against your goals; Supplement stack: every ingredient added up across the products you take; Stack check: over the limit, underdosed, hidden in a blend, or flagged by FDA or Health Canada; A guide to about 170 ingredients sold in North America, with the evidence for each; AI stack review for current recalls and safety alerts. Source: https://github.com/adervec/MacroTrackro (MIT).
- [Marksman](https://adervec.github.io/MarksmanApp/): Foam-dart marksmanship, measured — photograph your target and get real metrics. Features: Mark up a photo of where your darts landed — precision, accuracy, bias; Tiered practice standards judge every session; Progress overall, by blaster category, and by specific blaster; Prints true-size target faces to shoot at; Equipment packs: plain JSON defines drills, faces, and vocabulary. Source: https://github.com/adervec/MarksmanApp (MIT).
- [Run315](https://adervec.github.io/Run315/): GymTracker for cardio — every Garmin and Strava number you have, analysed properly. Features: Garmin and Strava arrive through a cowork folder, or a Garmin export archive; A fitness / fatigue model fitted to you, race projections, taper planning; Route builder, new-ground runs, trail completion, and a territory game; Replay, ghost races, records, year in review — and an SQL console over it all; No server, no account — press Load demo athlete to look around. Source: https://github.com/adervec/Run315 (MIT).
- [Learning Pit](https://adervec.github.io/learning-pit/): Flashcards and learning games with spaced repetition — for readers and pre-readers alike. Features: 23 modules from first words to full decks — plus make your own; Spaced repetition with sessions, streaks, exam mode, and undo; Games: match boards, duels, spelling, tracing on a slate; Kid mode with pictures, stickers, and read-aloud voices; Static files, no build — fully offline once installed. Source: https://github.com/adervec/learning-pit (MIT).
- [Music Studio](https://adervec.github.io/MusicStudio/): An ElevenLabs album builder in your browser — curate prompts, generate songs, export albums. Features: Albums in nested groups with full metadata and per-group themes; Generate songs, dialog, sound effects and stems — cost estimate first; Waveforms, trim/fade/gain, reorder, playlists, crossfaded mixdowns; Export tagged tracks — and publish picked albums to a phone-synced folder; Ratings, notes, and a taste profile an agent can read and design albums from. Source: https://github.com/adervec/MusicStudio (MIT).
- [The Long Gallery](https://adervec.github.io/long-gallery/): A museum in a single page — 9,300 works from the Olmec heads to now, each with its story. Features: Six eras, Antiquity to Modern, across movements, regions and themes; Every work with its story: what it is, its context, and a hidden detail; HD zoom on every credited plate, plus guided tours through the collection; A map of where each work hangs; artist pages with portraits and timelines; Autoplay: a hands-free walk, timed or narrated with subtitles. Source: https://github.com/adervec/long-gallery (MIT).
- [The Classical Journey](https://adervec.github.io/classical-journey/): Every piece worth hearing, in order — Gregorian chant to now, with what to listen for. Features: 8,300 works — the classical canon, plus a Journey for every other genre; Each one: what it is, the world it came from, and what to listen for; Theory stops, placed where history invented the idea; Autoplay with spoken notes, a gym mode, and a blind listening quiz; Piece of the day, a weekly mix, and listening-history import. Source: https://github.com/adervec/classical-journey (MIT).
- [InsightMaster](https://adervec.github.io/InsightMaster/): A meditation practice tracker whose timer teaches — it walks the technique step by step. Features: A guided timer: countdown ring, bells, and the current step called out in time; Open-ended sits, a settling-in countdown, vibration for silent sits; Plans, streaks, reminders, and stats on where the practice has gone; The content is data — ships with sitting meditation, replace it with your own; One file, no account; history exports to CSV. Source: https://github.com/adervec/InsightMaster (MIT).
- [Celebrity Crusher](https://adervec.github.io/CelebrityCrusher/): 389 celebrity fitness feats, judged against your own Strava and Garmin data. Features: Which feats you've already beaten, which you'd clear today, which are a plan; Fitness / fatigue, estimated VO₂max, and a marathon projection with a second opinion; Goals: feat + date becomes a week-by-week build, exportable to your calendar; Pace curve against every timed feat, Eddington numbers, a three-year forecast; Zero dependencies — the same app runs as a local server with live OAuth sync. Source: https://github.com/adervec/CelebrityCrusher (MIT).
- [LanguageLab](https://adervec.github.io/LanguageLab/): Learn a language by using it: listen, read, take dictation, speak, write. Progress is the level your numbers support, not a streak. Features: First steps from nothing in 44 languages: sixty lessons of phrases to hear, write and say, twelve lessons of words with pictures, and the letters of 14 scripts to practise; A sitting: hear a story, answer from the ear alone, read it, take dictation at natural speed, write a sentence back, speak, retell; Talk with an AI partner that corrects you as you go; role-plays said aloud and then from memory; an AI pen pal; Tap any word for its meaning; your own mistakes, and a teacher's corrections, come back as review cards; Bring a podcast with its subtitles and take dictation from the real voices; Graded stories and dialogues in all 44 languages, twelve or more in each; installs like an app and opens offline. Source: https://github.com/adervec/LanguageLab (MIT).

## Shared pieces

- [House standards](https://github.com/adervec/CoworkSyncHub/blob/main/HOUSE-STANDARDS.md): the rules every app follows (sync without overwrites, security, languages, themes, data inventory, accessibility), each with an automated check.
- [font.js](https://adervec.github.io/font.js): one script every app loads for the house font, themes, languages, About panel, backup, the reader's cloud with safe sync, and the session ledger.
- [cowork.js](https://adervec.github.io/cowork.js) and [the protocol](https://github.com/adervec/CoworkSyncHub/blob/main/COWORK-PROTOCOL.md): how an app hands work to an AI and reviews the answer.
- [The AI runner](https://github.com/adervec/CoworkSyncHub/blob/main/RUNNER.md): a small local program that answers apps' AI requests, merges Garmin and Strava, and writes a daily brief.
- [The portal](https://adervec.github.io/portal/): every app in one place.
